assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Atom
items.clue: The smallest part of an element that can exist.

items.label: Electron
items.clue: A negatively charged particle, relative charge −1, that occupies energy levels (shells) around the nucleus.

items.label: Fractional distillation
items.clue: A physical process that separates two or more miscible liquids using the differences between their boiling points.

items.label: Proton
items.clue: A positively charged particle in the nucleus; the positive charge of a nucleus is a whole number of these identical charges.

questions.stem: Which statement about scientific models is correct?

options.text: New experimental evidence may lead to a model being replaced
Once a model has been accepted it can no longer be changed
A model changes when a scientist prefers a different idea
A model that explains most results is never questioned

questions.explanation: This is the specification statement about how scientific models change.

questions.stem: What were atoms thought to be like before the electron was discovered?

options.text: Tiny spheres with a nucleus in the middle
Balls of negative charge holding protons
Spheres with electrons in set orbits
Tiny spheres that could not be divided

questions.explanation: Before the discovery of the electron, atoms were thought to be indivisible spheres.

questions.stem: Which statement describes the plum pudding model of the atom?

options.text: A ball of negative charge with positive particles inside it
A ball of positive charge with negative electrons embedded in it
A small positive nucleus with electrons around the outside
A solid sphere of matter that cannot be divided at all

questions.explanation: This is the specification's description of the plum pudding model.

questions.stem: What conclusion came from the results of the alpha particle scattering experiment?

options.text: The positive charge is spread evenly through the whole atom
The atom is a solid ball of matter with no gaps in it
Electrons in the atom deflect the alpha particles back
The mass of an atom is concentrated at a charged centre

questions.explanation: The results led to the conclusion that the mass is concentrated at a charged nucleus.

questions.stem: In the scattering experiment a few alpha particles were deflected straight back. Why did this change the atomic model?

options.text: It showed that the whole atom is filled with positive charge
It showed that electrons are far heavier than was thought
The plum pudding model could not explain such large deflections
It proved that atoms are tiny spheres that cannot be split

questions.explanation: A spread-out positive charge could not turn a fast alpha particle around.

questions.stem: What is the main difference between the plum pudding model and the nuclear model?

options.text: In the nuclear model the mass and charge are in the nucleus
In the plum pudding model the electrons orbit a small nucleus
In the nuclear model the electrons are embedded in positive charge
In the nuclear model the mass is spread evenly through the atom

questions.explanation: The nuclear model concentrates the mass and the positive charge at the centre.

questions.stem: What did Niels Bohr suggest, and how did his idea compare with experiment?

options.text: Electrons orbit at specific distances, and his calculations agreed with observations
Electrons orbit at specific distances, but no experimental observations supported this
The nucleus exists, and his calculations agreed with the observations
Electrons deflect the alpha particles, and this matched results

questions.explanation: Bohr adapted the nuclear model, and his theoretical calculations agreed with experimental observations.

questions.stem: What did later experiments show about the positive charge of a nucleus?

options.text: It can be divided into whole numbers of identical charges
It is carried by one single particle found by James Chadwick
It comes from the neutrons, which each carry a small charge
It is spread evenly through the atom, not in a nucleus

questions.explanation: Each of these identical smaller charges was named a proton.

questions.stem: What did the experimental work of James Chadwick provide evidence for?

options.text: Protons inside the nucleus, about 20 years after this was accepted
Neutrons inside the nucleus, about 20 years after it was accepted
Electrons, which had been found long before the nuclear model
The nucleus itself, at the centre of every atom

questions.explanation: Chadwick's work showed that neutrons exist within the nucleus.
